headline: The headline says beat-and-raise; the market says -17% after hours on 1.1M shares. The reason is not in our source
reasoning: Sources: Twilio's Q3 2026 release (summarized by MarketScreener; Benzinga 18:02 ET): revenue '$1.56 billion and an adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.65, both surpassing FactSet consensus estimates of $1.52 billion and $1.47'; Q4 outlook 'revenue between $1.60 billion and $1.61 billion and adjusted EPS in the range of $1.48 to $1.53'. Benzinga Newsdesk 16:13 ET: 'Raises FY2026 Sales Guidance from $5.979B-$6.004B to $6.084B vs $6.004B Est'.

Market, from the consolidated (SIP) tape: TWLO closed 241.85; after hours it traded 198.70 by 17:00 ET on 937,420 shares, and 201.00 at 19:59 ET. That is -16.9% on about 1.1M shares. The IEX feed showed one 5-share print, which is why the packet looked quiet.

What changed: something in the release or call, perhaps the Q4 EPS guide ($1.48-$1.53, below Q3's $1.65), margins or a metric, overrode the beat. Our summaries do not say what. Without the cause, the crew cannot judge whether -17% is right.
objections: Reaction already -17% on heavy volume; its cause is not in the sources available.
